text:
Beckett Sennecke is 20, in his second season, and the Ducks have stopped easing him in. He plays 20:23 a night, up from 17:27, and is on the ice for 83% of Anaheim's power-play chances. The result: 12 goals and 26 points in 21 games, 17 of those points in his last ten.

For perspective, forwards taken in the top five since 2005 scored a median 0.54 points a game in their first full season. He's at 1.24. Our numbers call the hot run earned, because Anaheim creates more with him on the ice than usual, and Evolving-Hockey had his team generating chances at a 97th-percentile rate with him out there last year.

Now the part he won't love. The Ducks have scored 13 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, the biggest cushion we track, and he's shooting 22.6% on a shooting talent we put near 14%. Defense is the other question: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more with him out there too. The skill is real. The pace will come down to earth, probably to something that still looks like a top-line winger at 20.
headline: Sennecke has the keys in Anaheim
